_comment: Hand-curated names and notes for what the game leaves numbered. Never generated; see CLAUDE.md. `kinds` names the block kinds, which the lattice's style values and the records' kind word share. `types` names what stands on a face: `by` names the field whose value tells a type's variants apart, each with its own name and, where it has one, colour and points; `facing` names the field that holds the way a thing points, as quarter turns on its face; `state` names the field that says whether a device a switch toggles starts on; and `points` is what collecting one scores. `levels` is keyed by pack path and index; a level's `score` is the most it scores where the disc holds more than can be collected, and its note says what is out of reach.

1.name: Fire block
1.note: A block whose every face is fire: touching it inflates the ball until it pops or reaches cooler ground.

2.name: Ice block
2.note: A block the ball slides across without stopping until it reaches a normal square or the edge.

3.name: Invisible block
3.note: A block that cannot be seen until the ball is close, or, on some levels, only from far away; sunglasses reveal it for a while.

4.name: Acid block
4.note: A green block painted with an acid splat, found only on the object catalogue level.

5.name: Moving platform
5.note: A platform that travels back and forth along a straight run, stopping briefly at each end.

6.name: Crumbling block
6.note: A block that disappears once rolled onto, leaving time for one move.

7.name: Vanishing block
7.note: A block that fades in and out of existence on a cycle.

8.name: Laser
8.note: A laser beam between two blocks. Its colour is its circuit: a switch of that colour turns it on and off, with the teleporters of the same colour, and a beam drawn broken starts switched off. The game puts a block at each end as the level loads, so an end can stand where the level itself has no block.

9.name: Level settings
9.note: Not a block but the level's settings, kept where a block would be, often on an empty cell. They mark a hidden level, which the game draws half-transparent with the glass ball, and on a few levels pull the camera further back.

666.name: Camera
666.note: Where the level's camera looks, and from what angles, with the level's time.

1.name: Fire
1.note: Fire on one face of an otherwise normal block; a block that is fire all over is a fire block instead.

2.name: Ice
2.note: Ice on one face of an otherwise normal block.

5.name: Teleporter
5.note: Rolling onto one carries the ball to another of the same colour; a switch of that colour turns the pair on and off.

7.name: Exit
7.note: Red until every key is collected, then green; touching it ends the level.

8.name: Clock
8.note: A square that freezes the timer while the ball sits on it.

9.name: Switch
9.note: A button that turns every laser and teleporter of its colour on and off.

10.name: Boost button
10.note: Launches the ball three squares forward, or two forward and one up.

11.name: Moving spikes
11.note: Spikes that rise and retract in turn, each from its own point in the cycle; safe to roll over when down.

12.name: Spikes
12.note: Pops the ball on touch; jump over them.

26.name: Hidden exit
26.note: Appears once every key is collected, colourless, and leads to the world's hidden level.

28.name: Arrow
28.note: A square the ball can only leave in the direction the arrow points.

29.name: Start on a clock
29.note: The block and face the ball starts the level on, a clock rather than a plain square.

30.name: Start
30.note: The block and face the ball starts the level on.

31.name: Key
31.note: Collecting every key on a level opens the exit, which turns from red to green.

32.name: Lethargy pill
32.note: Slows the ball, rocks the screen and runs the timer fast for fifteen seconds.

33.name: Bouncy pill
33.note: Makes every forward move a two-square bounce and a jump three, until the level ends.

34.note: Only on the object catalogue level, so nothing in play uses it.

35.name: Hourglass
35.note: Flips the timer, and scores 1200 less twelve times the seconds left, so 1190 at best.

36.name: Gem
36.note: Blue, green or red, and worth the same whatever the colour.

37.name: Coin
37.note: Three tiers told apart by colour: bronze is worth 250, blue 500 and gold 750.

38.name: Sunglasses
38.note: Reveals invisible blocks for a while.

42.note: Only on the object catalogue level, so nothing in play uses it.

43.name: Fruit
43.note: Five fruit come round in turn, apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry, and collecting all five earns a bonus level.

44.name: Fruit
44.note: Five fruit come round in turn, apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry, and collecting all five earns a bonus level.

45.name: Fruit
45.note: Five fruit come round in turn, apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry, and collecting all five earns a bonus level.

46.name: Fruit
46.note: Five fruit come round in turn, apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry, and collecting all five earns a bonus level.

47.name: Fruit
47.note: Five fruit come round in turn, apple, watermelon, pumpkin, bananas and strawberry, and collecting all five earns a bonus level.

50.name: Captivator
50.note: A spiked star that restarts the level on touch: the thinner one, with three long points, which travels the space it has and turns back at any wall or object in its way.

51.name: Rolling stone
51.note: A grey cylinder that rolls slowly round a set course and can be jumped over.

52.name: Captivator
52.note: A spiked star that restarts the level on touch: the fuller one, with four short points, which slides back and forth over a fixed stretch, as if on a spring.

53.name: Captivator, wandering
53.note: A blue hexagonal ball that shakes, then moves one square in a random direction; the way it shakes gives away where it is going.

56.name: Captivator, bouncing
56.note: A corkscrew that bounces up and down: roll under it when it is up, and jump it when it is down.

/HIRO/HIRO.PAK#19.note: The training level the Japanese release lists as Lesson on its main menu, with one of nearly everything the game has on one floor. The other two releases keep it on the disc but off the menu.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#15.note: The disc holds 3500 more, the twelve coins on the corners of the lowest ring: they and the four gems inside that ring cannot both be had, and the gems score more. The Japanese release removes the coins.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#18.note: The best known score, and not a certain one: it takes the coin under the exit block, which the Japanese release removes as unreachable, and leaves one of the ten crumbling blocks, the 50 more the disc holds.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#19.note: The developers' object catalogue: one of nearly every object in the game, laid out on a flat floor. It ships unchanged in nine of the ten worlds, and nothing in the game leads to it.

/HILLS/HILLSFI.PAK#0.note: The Final has no fruit, and the PAL release put an apple on this level anyway, which the US and Japanese releases removed, leaving the blue teleporter it stood beside with nothing to reach.

/INCA/INCA.PAK#9.note: The disc holds 100 more, two crumbling blocks that cannot be reached.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#7.note: The disc holds 100 more, two of the five crumbling blocks, which the best known route leaves standing.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#10.note: The Japanese release un-iced one face of the solid ice block for an arrow that nothing can reach, and removed the blue coin on the same block, which can be collected here.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#11.note: The hidden exit at 14,19,18 stands on a block that cannot be reached once it has appeared. The PAL release forgot to place it, and the Japanese release moved it to LEVEL 134, the one release in which every hidden level can be played.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#12.note: The Japanese release moved one of the gems off the lethal tile it stands on here onto a kinder one.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#13.note: The Japanese release moves the world's hidden exit to this level.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#16.note: The disc holds 8925 more, three gems under the three far blocks, which only the bouncy pill reaches and which the pill then keeps you from collecting; the Japanese release removes them.

/MARS/MARS.PAK#18.note: The only hidden level with a fruit, at 9,18,15, which the Japanese release removed; in this release the exit that leads here is out of reach.
